Everyday batteries & power markets

Everyday battery value comparison

Compare Daiso, Energizer, Duracell and Bexel prices and runtime under the same test conditions.

How much does a lower price help?

In its June 2024 test of 14 products, the Korea Consumer Agency found that Daiso NeoCell combined a low purchase price with good runtime. The largest differences in runtime per cell were 1.3× for AAA and 1.2× for AA. However, runtime for the same KRW 100 was up to 8.6× greater for AAA NeoCell and 7.1× for AA NeoCell than the least cost-effective products tested. These maximum differences span the full test set, not a specific one-to-one comparison with Energizer.

The 2024 test is not a current price list. Prices below were paid at physical stores in January 2024. Discounts, pack sizes and product changes can alter today's value comparison.

Choosing between Daiso and Energizer

In the AAA low-drain test, NeoCell and Energizer Max both rated Excellent. Their historical per-cell prices were KRW 200 and about KRW 1,092, a difference of approximately 5.46×. A 5.46× price difference does not mean a 5.46× runtime difference. NeoCell was a cost-effective choice for everyday low- and medium-drain uses.

In the AA portable-light test, NeoCell rated Good, while Duracell Deluxe, Duracell Ultra and Bexel Platinum rated Excellent. Consider replacement frequency, required power, storage time and purchase discounts. This test does not guarantee performance in every high-drain device or long-term protection against leakage. All tested products met the leakage and heavy-metal test criteria.

Daiso being a Korean retailer does not mean its products are manufactured in Korea. A product sold domestically is not automatically Korean-made.
